A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BAO study and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–D. Retained material can be matched reliably despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original BAO experiments on Function-Gym, Telepathy-Gym and Turtle-Gym, including component ablations, exploration measurements and reward-hacking analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds penalty-weight sensitivity tests and an alternative-teacher experiment in Appendix A.2–A.3.

M1.justification: The behavior-enhanced SFT and behavior-regularized GRPO pipeline, behavior categories, prompts and Algorithm 1 are retained. v2 newly specifies w=0 and an initial-turn failure penalty as implementation details; this does not establish a revision to the underlying procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same three UserRL tasks and feedback environments. The new appendix experiments vary penalty settings and the demonstration teacher within existing task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains exactly the same commercial models, raw Qwen3 models, UserRL baselines and BAO variants. The added teacher experiment retains UserRL as the comparator; GPT-4o-mini serves as a demonstration teacher.

E3.justification: Appendix A.2 adds Function-Gym sweeps of λans from 0.0005 to 0.005 and λthink from 0.005 to 0.05. Appendix A.3 adds a Telepathy-Gym/Qwen3-1.7B comparison using GPT-4o-mini demonstrations with matched SFT counts and RL data. Existing experiment settings are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.2–A.3 tests sensitivity to both regularization coefficients and dependence on teacher capability. These are targeted additions to the existing component ablations, exploration analyses, reward-hacking tests and case studies.

E5.justification: Figure 5 retains its three-random-seed averages and standard-deviation shading. The new appendix tables provide point estimates without adding run counts, uncertainty estimates or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the existing plotted results are unchanged; new Tables 2–4 add sensitivity and alternative-teacher results. Under the new GPT-4o-mini-teacher setting, BAO versus UserRL achieves Pass@U-1 of 0.5122 versus 0.1707 and UR of 0.1423 versus 0.7619. These are additional-condition results, not revised original scores.

T1.justification: The contextual MDP, action-space decomposition, reward and engagement definitions, and Equations 1–5 remain mathematically unchanged apart from notation clarification. The rewritten Pareto discussion adds no substantive formal assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The same core contributions remain: the multi-objective formulation, retrospective and prospective behaviors, BAO training, and improved performance–engagement trade-offs. v2 foregrounds the Pareto framing in the abstract without materially changing these claims or the conclusion.

C2.justification: Section 3 adds sparse reward signals as an explanation for unsuccessful naive reward balancing. Appendix A.2 interprets λans variation as a smooth engagement–score trade-off, while A.3 addresses dependence on teacher capability. Existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents w=0, a 0.5 penalty for failing to complete initial-turn generation within the token budget, and numerical regularization settings in the new ablations. Existing training configurations, prompts, software, hardware and access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 removes the Rahimi et al. (2025) citation and reference. It also explicitly contrasts BAO's inter-turn behavior emphasis with handcrafted reward balancing in Sun et al. (2025) and CollabLLM, while retaining the broader related-work discussion.

P1.justification: The abstract, parts of the introduction, Section 3 and the opening of Section 4 are rewritten to clarify the Pareto framing. Two appendix subsections, acknowledgments and affiliation/publication-header edits are added; the overall organization remains intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 reorders its panels and adds an annotated infeasible region. Three appendix tables are added, existing configuration tables become Tables 5–6, and several figures relocate within the main text. The other displays retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: The new penalty-sensitivity and teacher controls in Appendix A.2–A.3 strengthen empirical support, while the explicit implementation details improve reproducibility. These gains are bounded by their selected task/model settings; the main results and conclusions remain unchanged. The evidence supports a modest overall improvement.
